lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: recurring obligations across a year

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recurring obligations across a year task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given four provided obligation categories (a housing-type payment, a utility-type payment, a subscription, and an annual renewal), the learner assigns each an invented recurring month or months across a blank twelve-month calendar, then identifies any month carrying an unusually heavy invented load.
safetyNotes: All obligations and their months are invented for this practice; no real bill, account, or payment amount is required.
materials: learner-local: a blank twelve-month calendar grid (paper or digital)
learner-local: the four provided obligation categories

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was your warm-up prediction correct? What did seeing it laid out on the calendar change about your thinking?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Calendar completeness: All four categories appear on the calendar with a plausible invented recurrence. | Smoothing proposal: A specific heaviest month is named with a workable smoothing idea. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a fifth, self-chosen obligation category of their own invention and recalculate whether it changes which month is heaviest.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic recurring obligations across a year task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given four provided obligation categories (a housing-type payment, a utility-type payment, a subscription, and an annual renewal), the learner assigns each an invented recurring month or months across a blank twelve-month calendar, then identifies any month carrying an unusually heavy invented load.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recurring obligations across a year decision or action.
Model move 2: Before filling in the calendar, predict which time of year might end up the heaviest.
Model move 3: Place each of the four obligation categories onto the twelve-month calendar with an invented recurrence.

Model check: Calendar completeness: All four categories appear on the calendar with a plausible invented recurrence. | Smoothing proposal: A specific heaviest month is named with a workable smoothing idea.

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recurring obligations across a year.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given four provided obligation categories (a housing-type payment, a utility-type payment, a subscription, and an annual renewal), the learner assigns each an invented recurring month or months across a blank twelve-month calendar, then identifies any month carrying an unusually heavy invented load.
Coach direction: Before filling in the calendar, predict which time of year might end up the heaviest.
Learner prompt: Before you fill anything in, which time of year do you predict will end up carrying the most obligations, and why?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Place each of the four obligation categories onto the twelve-month calendar with an invented recurrence.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I placed the housing-type payment on the calendar with a monthly or other invented recurrence.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I placed the utility-type payment on the calendar.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I placed the subscription and the annual renewal on the calendar.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was your warm-up prediction correct? What did seeing it laid out on the calendar change about your thinking?

Success checks: Calendar completeness: All four categories appear on the calendar with a plausible invented recurrence. | Smoothing proposal: A specific heaviest month is named with a workable smoothing idea.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recurring obligations across a year supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recurring obligations across a year condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Calendar completeness: All four categories appear on the calendar with a plausible invented recurrence. | Smoothing proposal: A specific heaviest month is named with a workable smoothing idea..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: recurring obligations across a year — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
